summary: Sidecar cohort flood causing transient GPU attach gap in customer's dedicated pool
description: Issue summary: Customer reports recurring midday throughput plateaus and transient allocation failures on their dedicated GPU pool. Symptoms surface as batches queueing for several seconds, followed by a short window where new connections fail to attach and 429s spike on tenant routes. Impact: Nimbus Health production inference saw p95 latency double and automatic fallback to smaller model variants 12 times in the past 48 hours. Several critical clinical workflows experienced degraded response time but no data loss. Environment: Dedicated pool (prod:us-west-2), tenant namespace: nimbus-health-prod, worker fleet: dedicated-a3-8, sidecar agent version: 1.4.7, autoscaler version: 2.3.1. Observed time window: weekdays 11:30 - 13:15 PST.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Have steady background traffic (small embeddings + short chat streams). 2) Trigger a coordinated analytics sidecar job from the customer that opens ~400 short-lived keepalive connections (observed in customer logs). 3) Within 30-90s, allocator attach latency spikes, new session attach calls return 504/429 intermittently. 4) Recovery occurs after ~120-300s as sidecar connections drain and autoscaler reacts.

investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: short-lived sidecar connection storm from customer analytics causing allocator to exhaust attach concurrency and scheduler to transiently fail allocation handshakes.
Checked node-level GPU utilization during window: overall GPU utilization was moderate (~55-70%) but attach rate and NVLink attach queues reported contention spikes.
Autoscaler telemetry shows delayed upscale: scale decision latency was ~45s after threshold due to metric sampling granularity. This allowed a short attach gap before new replicas became available.
We observed sidecar agent threads holding file descriptors and TLS sessions open longer than expected (sidecar 1.4.7), amplifying connection fan-in beyond typical production patterns.
Cross-checked with infra: no underlying driver crashes or HBM OOM recorded; GPU memory pressure remained low. Indicates allocation handshake contention rather than raw GPU exhaustion.
Correlated customer-side logs show a scheduled analytics job opening many ephemeral keepalives exactly at the start of the window.
customer_communication: 2026-03-08 09:12 - Leah Martinez (Support): Thanks for reporting. Can you confirm whether an analytics job runs during the 11:30 window and provide last 24h sidecar logs?

2026-03-08 11:05 - Nimbus Health (Ops): Confirmed — a nightly analytics sampler also runs at 11:30; attaching snippet of their sidecar controlplane. They say it's short-lived connections for telemetry sampling.
2026-03-09 14:20 - Arjun Patel (Eng): We're investigating attach timing and autoscaler sampling. Asking SRE to pull allocator attach histograms for us for the 11:30 window.
2026-03-10 16:03 - Support (Leah): Shared recommended temporary mitigation: throttle sidecar sampler to 50 concurrent connections and enable prefix KV caching for high-frequency embedding routes.
timeline: 2026-03-08 - Ticket created after customer reported recurring midday degradation.
2026-03-09 - Initial triage: support reproduced attach gap in staging with synthetic sidecar flood.
2026-03-10 - Engineering gathered allocator and autoscaler telemetry and confirmed sampling lag contributes to the window.
2026-03-11 - Deployed customer-side temporary mitigation and requested follow-up metrics; ongoing monitoring scheduled.
temporary_workarounds: Ask customer to stagger analytics sampler or cap concurrent keepalives to <= 80 connections (they reduced from ~400 to 60 and reported immediate improvement).
Enable aggressive KV/prefix caching on embedding endpoints to reduce attach frequency for repeated short requests.
Apply autoscaler sampling policy override for this dedicated pool: reduce metric aggregation window from 30s to 10s (temporary).
root_cause: Combination of customer-side ephemeral connection fan-in (sidecar cohort), allocator attach handshake contention, and autoscaler metric sampling granularity led to a short-lived attach gap despite available GPU compute. Not a raw GPU memory exhaustion; rather attach throughput and scheduling coupling to sidecar behavior.
resolution_notes: Customer applied recommended sampler cap and saw p95 latency return to baseline within one recovery window.
Deployed autoscaler sampling tweak to the affected pool to accelerate scale decisions while we validate a long-term fix.
Created engineering follow-up ticket to harden allocator attach path (PR linked) and to add protective backpressure when ephemeral connection fan-in is detected.
Suggested long-term customer action: migrate analytics sampler to a separate tenant or schedule it outside of production peak windows.
Next steps: ENG to land allocator handshake improvements (PR #3221), SRE to add dashboard alert for attach queue depth, CS to coordinate with customer on permanent scheduling change.
follow_up_tasks: INT-9001 - Run allocator attach stress test with sidecar cohorts and collect attach latency percentiles across GPU types.
ENG-447 - Improve allocator backpressure and add circuit-breaker on connect storms (linked PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/3221).
SRE-210 - Add attach-queue-depth metric to per-pool dashboards and firing rule for >200ms median attach over 1m.
CS-51 - Confirm customer scheduling change and close once three business days of stable telemetry are observed.
